summary.text: The Holocene Climate Optimum was a warm stretch from roughly 9,500 to 5,500 years ago, with its peak around 8,000 years ago.
It was about 4.9 °C warmer than the Last Glacial Maximum and was followed by a slow cooling of about 0.1 to 0.3 °C per thousand years until about two centuries ago.
The warmth was uneven: Svalbard, near the North Pole, ran about 6 °C above today, while the tropics and parts of the Southern Hemisphere were colder than average.

items.prompt: How did the planet's average temperature during the warmest 200 years of this period compare with the 2011–2019 average?

options.label: About 5 °C warmer
About 1 °C warmer
About 0.3 °C cooler
About 3 °C cooler

items.explain: A 2020 study put the warmest 200 years, around 6,500 years ago, about 0.3 °C below the 2011–2019 average.

items.prompt: Where did temperatures climb the most during this warm period?

options.label: Along the equator in the tropics
Across the Southern Hemisphere
Evenly, in every part of Earth
In the far north, near the Pole

items.explain: The change fell off quickly with latitude: Svalbard was about 6 °C warmer than now, while low and middle latitudes saw essentially no change.

items.prompt: Much of Central Asia is desert today. What was it like during this warm period?

options.label: Mostly forest, thanks to more rain
Even drier, with larger sand dunes
Buried under thick ice sheets
Flooded by a broad shallow sea

items.explain: Higher rainfall meant today's desert regions of Central Asia were extensively forested.

items.prompt: In the Middle East, this period brought frost-free winters and rich savannas. What changed in human life there during the same stretch?

options.label: People abandoned the region for colder lands
Cereals were domesticated and populations grew
Crops failed and settled villages emptied out
Iron tools spread quickly from town to town

items.explain: The domestication of cereals and Neolithic population growth in the region happened during this interval.

items.prompt: Northwestern North America warmed early in this period, but the northeast reached its peak about 4,000 years later. What held the east back?

options.label: Volcanic ash that blocked out the sunlight
Cold winds blowing in from the Pacific
A leftover ice sheet that kept it chilled
Thick forests that reflected away the sun

items.explain: While the northwest peaked, the Laurentide Ice Sheet was still chilling eastern Canada.

items.prompt: During this period the East Asian summer monsoon rains pushed deep into the heart of Asia. What allowed them to reach so far?

options.label: New mountain ranges lifting moist air inland
Rising seas and shrinking northern ice sheets
Volcanic eruptions in Japan seeding clouds
A weaker summer sun over the Pacific Ocean

items.explain: Rising sea levels and the decay of Northern Hemisphere ice sheets let the monsoon rain belt expand northwest into the Asian interior.
